plans.title: Myocardial Infarction (MI)
plans.summary: Acute coronary syndrome — relieving pain and protecting the myocardium.

diagnoses.related: related to myocardial ischemia from decreased coronary blood flow
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by crushing chest pain radiating to the arm/jaw, diaphoresis, and anxiety
subjective: States “it feels like an elephant on my chest.”
outcomes: Client reports chest pain relieved to ≤2/10 and shows no ECG signs of ongoing ischemia.

interventions.i: Assess pain and obtain a 12-lead ECG.
interventions.r: Guides treatment and confirms ischemia/infarct location.

interventions.i: Administer aspirin, oxygen (if hypoxic), nitroglycerin, and morphine as ordered.
interventions.r: MONA reduces clot burden, ischemia, and oxygen demand.

interventions.i: Maintain continuous cardiac monitoring.
Provide rest and a calm environment.

diagnoses.evaluation: Chest pain relieved to 1/10; no new ST-segment changes; client resting comfortably.

diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by dysrhythmias, hypotension, and fatigue
outcomes: Client maintains adequate cardiac output with stable vital signs and no lethal dysrhythmias.

interventions.i: Monitor vital signs, rhythm, and urine output.
Administer beta-blockers and ACE inhibitors as prescribed.
Limit activity per orders.

diagnoses.evaluation: Vital signs stable; no lethal dysrhythmias; adequate urine output maintained.

plans.title: Stroke (CVA)
plans.summary: Mobility and swallowing safety after a cerebrovascular accident.

diagnoses.related: related to neuromuscular impairment from the stroke
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by hemiparesis and decreased range of motion
outcomes: Client maintains joint function and skin integrity and participates in rehabilitation.

interventions.i: Perform range-of-motion exercises and reposition regularly.
Collaborate with physical and occupational therapy.
Use safety measures and assistive devices.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client maintained full ROM without contractures and engaged in PT.

diagnoses.related: related to neuromuscular deficit affecting the swallow reflex
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by coughing with intake and a facial droop
outcomes: Client swallows safely without signs of aspiration.

interventions.i: Keep NPO until a swallow screen is passed.
Position upright at 90° for meals and 30 min after.
interventions.r: Uses gravity to protect the airway.

interventions.i: Provide prescribed thickened liquids/modified diet; keep suction ready.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client passed the swallow screen and tolerated a modified diet without aspiration.

plans.title: Chronic Kidney Disease
plans.summary: Fluid balance and nutrition in declining kidney function.

diagnoses.related: related to decreased glomerular filtration and sodium/water retention
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by edema, hypertension, and rapid weight gain
subjective: Reports swelling and shortness of breath
outcomes: Client achieves euvolemia with stable weight and clear lungs.

interventions.i: Monitor daily weight, I&O, and edema.
interventions.r: Tracks fluid status and therapy response.

interventions.i: Enforce fluid and sodium restriction as ordered.
Monitor potassium and phosphorus.
Prepare for/support dialysis as prescribed.

diagnoses.evaluation: Weight and blood pressure decreased toward baseline; lungs clear; potassium in range.

diagnoses.related: related to dietary restrictions, anorexia, and uremia
outcomes: Client maintains adequate nutrition within renal dietary limits.

interventions.i: Provide a renal diet (limited protein, potassium, phosphorus, sodium).
Give phosphate binders with meals.
Consult a renal dietitian.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client maintained weight and phosphorus improved with binder use.

plans.title: Major Depression
plans.summary: Safety and coping for major depressive disorder.

diagnoses.related: related to hopelessness, depressed mood, and expressed worthlessness
subjective: States “everyone would be better off without me.”
outcomes: Client remains safe and free from self-harm and verbalizes reasons for living.

interventions.i: Ask directly about suicidal ideation, plan, and means.
interventions.r: Direct questioning does not increase risk and identifies danger.

interventions.i: Ensure a safe environment and appropriate observation (1:1 if indicated); remove means.
Establish a therapeutic, nonjudgmental relationship.
Administer antidepressants; monitor for increased energy early in treatment.
interventions.r: Risk can rise as energy returns before mood lifts.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client remained safe with no self-harm and identified supports and reasons for living.

diagnoses.related: related to a perceived inability to change one's situation
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by passive affect and verbalizations of despair
outcomes: Client verbalizes increased hope and participates in the plan of care.

interventions.i: Encourage expression of feelings and set small, achievable goals.
interventions.r: Builds a sense of control and accomplishment.

interventions.i: Provide structure and positive reinforcement.
Involve support systems.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client engaged in activities and expressed cautious optimism.

plans.title: Postpartum Care (Hemorrhage Risk)
plans.summary: Preventing and catching early postpartum hemorrhage.

diagnoses.related: related to uterine atony and birth trauma
subjective: Reports feeling a large gush with position changes
outcomes: Client maintains a firm, midline fundus with normal lochia and stable vital signs.

interventions.i: Assess fundal tone, height, and position frequently.
interventions.r: A boggy uterus is the leading cause of early PPH.

interventions.i: Massage the fundus if boggy and ensure the bladder is empty.
interventions.r: Stimulates contraction; a full bladder displaces the uterus.

interventions.i: Quantify lochia and monitor vital signs for shock.
Administer oxytocics as prescribed.

diagnoses.evaluation: Fundus firm and midline; lochia within normal limits; vital signs stable.

diagnoses.related: related to birth trauma and invasive procedures
outcomes: Client remains free of infection with normal temperature and healing tissues.

interventions.i: Teach perineal hygiene (front to back) and hand washing.
Monitor temperature and lochia for foul odor.
Teach signs of infection to report.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client remained afebrile with a clean, healing perineum.

plans.title: Pediatric Asthma
plans.summary: Managing an acute asthma exacerbation in a child and teaching the family.

diagnoses.related: related to bronchospasm and airway inflammation
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by wheezing, retractions, and tachypnea
subjective: Child says “I can’t catch my breath.”
outcomes: Child achieves an effective breathing pattern with clear breath sounds and SpO₂ ≥94%.

interventions.i: Position upright and provide calm reassurance.
interventions.r: Eases work of breathing; anxiety worsens bronchospasm.

interventions.i: Administer a short-acting bronchodilator (albuterol), then corticosteroids as ordered.
interventions.r: Bronchodilator opens airways first; steroids reduce inflammation.

interventions.i: Monitor respiratory status, SpO₂, and peak flow.
Provide oxygen as prescribed.

diagnoses.evaluation: Wheezing resolved; SpO₂ ≥94%; child breathing comfortably.

diagnoses.related: related to unfamiliarity with asthma management
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by incorrect inhaler technique and unrecognized triggers
subjective: Parent unsure when to use each inhaler
outcomes: Family correctly demonstrates inhaler technique and states the asthma action plan.

interventions.i: Teach and verify inhaler and spacer technique.
Review trigger avoidance and the written asthma action plan.
interventions.r: Prevents and guides response to attacks.

interventions.i: Teach when to seek emergency care.

diagnoses.evaluation: Family demonstrated correct technique and verbalized the action plan.

diagnoses.related: related to a perceived threat or situational crisis
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by restlessness, tachycardia, and expressed apprehension
subjective: States “I feel like something bad is going to happen.”
outcomes: Client reports reduced anxiety and demonstrates effective coping techniques.

interventions.i: Stay with the client and use a calm, reassuring approach.
Reduce environmental stimuli.
Teach relaxation and deep-breathing techniques.
Administer anxiolytics as prescribed for severe anxiety.
interventions.r: Provides short-term relief while coping skills develop.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client's heart rate normalized and they used breathing techniques to self-calm.

plans.title: Cirrhosis
plans.summary: Managing ascites and bleeding/encephalopathy risk in liver failure.

diagnoses.related: related to portal hypertension and hypoalbuminemia
diagnoses.aeb: as evidenced by ascites, peripheral edema, and weight gain
subjective: Reports abdominal fullness and tight clothing
outcomes: Client achieves reduced ascites with decreasing abdominal girth and stable respiratory status.

interventions.i: Measure daily weight and abdominal girth.
Restrict sodium and fluids; administer diuretics (often spironolactone).
Administer albumin and prepare for paracentesis as ordered.
Position in semi-Fowler's.
interventions.r: Eases breathing with a distended abdomen.

diagnoses.evaluation: Abdominal girth decreased and breathing eased with therapy.

diagnoses.related: related to impaired clotting, esophageal varices, and hepatic encephalopathy
subjective: Family reports the client seems confused
outcomes: Client remains free of injury with intact mentation and no active bleeding.

interventions.i: Monitor for GI bleeding; use a soft toothbrush and avoid trauma.
interventions.r: Varices and clotting defects raise bleeding risk.

interventions.i: Administer lactulose and monitor level of consciousness.
interventions.r: Lactulose lowers ammonia; LOC reflects encephalopathy.

interventions.i: Avoid hepatotoxic drugs and alcohol.

diagnoses.evaluation: Client remained free of bleeding; ammonia decreased and mentation improved with lactulose.
